candidates.title: uarch-step verifiers (regenerated Solidity referee and C++ replay) accept uarch stores that the native uarch refuses as traps, including stores into the PMA array, the shadow TLB and HTIF MMIO at fixed protocol addresses
candidates.component: machine-solidity-step regenerated (UArchStep.sol executeSD/SW/SH/SB -> EmulatorCompat.writeWord -> AccessLogs.writeWord); C++ uarch_replay_state_access (verify_step_uarch); native uarch_state_access/machine::write_word for comparison
candidates.role: Referee verifier (regenerated machine-solidity-step, also inside Dave's CartesiStateTransition); the C++ verify_step_uarch is Support (off-chain verifier)
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/regenerated-patched/src/EmulatorCompat.sol:127 writeWord and src/AccessLogs.sol:146 writeWord (no check of the target address against the uarch memory map); src/uarch-replay-state-access.hpp:358 do_write_word -> check_write_word_access (no address check); native refusal in src/machine.cpp:2030-2075 machine::write_word (unknown shadow register offset, non-memory range, host-read-only range, pmas_is_protected range all throw)
candidates.description: The native uarch (uarch_state_access -> machine::write_word) treats a uarch store to (a) an unknown offset of the processor or uarch shadow, (b) a non-memory range (HTIF/CLINT/PLIC MMIO, the empty sentinel above every range), (c) a host-read-only range (the PMA array at 0x10000) or (d) a protected range (the shadow TLB at 0x1000-0x6fff, shadow state) as an error: log_step_uarch and run_uarch throw, i.e. a uarch trap ('an access that its memory map does not allow', R3). Both verifiers replay the same store as an ordinary word write with a valid Merkle proof and accept it, producing an after-hash in which the PMA entries, a shadow TLB slot or an HTIF MMIO word hold arbitrary values. For (b) at fixed device addresses, (c) and (d), the condition is decided by the authenticated store address plus protocol constants (the board map is fixed by the manual: shadow TLB 0x1000-0x6fff, PMA array 0x10000-0x10fff, HTIF 0x40008000), so the log already authenticates the trap and R3 requires refusal. For stores into ranges whose presence depends on the machine configuration (e.g. an unmapped address), detection would need extra state, and R3 rates acceptance High as well. Note this lets an accepted transition rewrite PMA entries and shadow TLB slots (cached/derived fields of R10) by a plain store, which no other path can produce.
candidates.trigger: A dishonest claimant in a uarch-level match supplies, at the disputed uarch step, a before-state in which the uarch is about to execute sd/sw/sh/sb to one of these addresses (only possible from an unreachable before-state, see reachability), with a log/proof that the verifier accepts.
candidates.reachability: Unreachable from a valid template as far as reviewed: the pristine uarch program (uarch/uarch-bridge-state-access.hpp) writes main-machine memory only through ua_aliased_aligned_write after the interpreter's PMA checks (guest stores to the PMA array, shadow TLB or MMIO raise access faults or go through device emulation that updates shadow registers at known offsets), writes TLB slots only through the write-TLB ecall, writes shadow registers at their known offsets, and keeps its stack and data in uarch RAM. So the before-state needs uarch registers/RAM that no input sequence produces (the uarch is reset to the pristine state at every mcycle boundary of a valid template). If any reachable state made the pristine uarch perform such a store, that would itself be a Critical uarch trap (R3/R4), and the verifier would additionally accept a successor the honest operator cannot log.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies; the trigger is a proof from a dishonest claimant (in scope, section 4 'Logs and proofs are adversarial'), not an API call, snapshot, or A1-A8 violation. 2 Role: the regenerated machine-solidity-step is 'Referee verifier' in the AUDIT.md table; the C++ verify is Support. 3 High/Medium: R3: 'The uarch traps when it executes ... an access that its memory map does not allow' and 'A verifier refuses a trap whenever the log it receives already authenticates the condition. ... A verifier that accepts a trap its log does not authenticate has a High defect (section 8), because the acceptance matters only from an unreachable before-state.' Section 8 High: 'A verifier that misbehaves only on demonstrably unreachable before-states. Misbehaving means ... accepting a wrong or second after-hash (such as accepting a uarch trap, R3)'. The before-state is unreachable (argument above) -> High. Also R10: 'Such disagreements are semantics (R3), not log defects' - the verifier defines a successor where the transition function defines none. 4 Critical: not applicable unless a reachable state makes the pristine uarch store there. 5 Low: n/a. Claimed: High (referee verifier).
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not break the goal by itself (needs an unreachable before-state), but removes the margin R3 relies on: the referee verifier defines successors (including arbitrary rewrites of PMA entries and shadow TLB slots) for uarch traps that the honest operator's uarch refuses to log, so any future reachable path to such a store would make the referee accept a dishonest after-hash the honest operator cannot even dispute with a proof.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R10/trapstore.lua (baremetal-minimal config; uarch pc=0x600000 with 'sd x2,0(x1)', x1=A, via write_reg/write_memory; log crafted from get_proof siblings and patched after each write; sanity: for A=0x80000100 and 0x7ff00000 the crafted log equals the native one). Results: A=0x00fffffffffffff8: native REFUSED ('attempted memory write to sentinel'), C++ verify ACCEPTED, EVM StepVerifier.step ACCEPTED; A=0x10000: native REFUSED ('write to read-only PMAs'), C++ ACCEPTED, EVM ACCEPTED; A=0x40008000: native REFUSED ('write to HTIF device'), C++ ACCEPTED, EVM ACCEPTED; A=0x1000: native REFUSED ('protected memory range shadow state'), C++ ACCEPTED, EVM ACCEPTED.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: load baremetal-minimal, set uarch_pc to a uarch-RAM word holding 'sd x2,0(x1)' and x1=0x10000 (PMA array) or 0x1000 (shadow TLB); assert pcall(m.log_step_uarch) fails (native trap); craft the log as in trapstore.lua and assert that both machine:verify_step_uarch and the EVM harness e:step reject it; exit 1 while either accepts.

candidates.title: Off-by-one in Memory.validateStrideLength makes the Solidity referee verifier reject any uarch access to the last 32-byte leaf of the address space, which the native uarch and the C++ verifier accept
candidates.component: machine-solidity-step Memory.sol (released v0.17.0-test1 and regenerated; used by Dave's CartesiStateTransition through UArchStep/AccessLogs)
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/regenerated-patched/src/Memory.sol:98-104 validateStrideLength: 'assert(Stride.unwrap(stride) * s < MAX_STRIDE)' with MAX_STRIDE = MAX_SIZE - 1 = 2^59-1 (line 66); reached from AccessLogs.readWord/writeWord (src/AccessLogs.sol:121,146) via Memory.regionFromStride. Same code in work/solidity-step/released/src/Memory.sol:103.
candidates.description: A single-leaf region at stride 2^59-1 (byte addresses 0xffffffffffffffe0..0xffffffffffffffff) satisfies stride*s = 2^59-1, which is not < MAX_STRIDE, so the assert fails (Panic 0x01) and the whole step reverts. The correct bound is stride*s + s <= MAX_SIZE (equivalently stride*s <= MAX_SIZE - s); for s >= 2 the existing check happens to be right, so only the last leaf is affected. The C++ verifier (make_proof/bubble_up over a 64-bit tree) accepts the same access, and the native uarch reads 0 there (machine::read_memory pads with zeros beyond the last range). A uarch load with an address in that leaf thus has a defined successor in the native uarch and the C++ verifier, but the referee verifier rejects every proof of it: a semantic transition turned into a rejection (R3), and an outcome that depends on which implementation of the verifier is used (R2/R10).
candidates.trigger: A uarch-level dispute at a before-state where the uarch executes a load (ld/lw/lwu/lh/lhu/lb/lbu) whose effective address lies in the last leaf (e.g. x1 = 0xfffffffffffffff8, 'ld x2,0(x1)'). The honest party can log it (native accepts) but cannot get it accepted on-chain.
candidates.reachability: Unreachable from a valid template as far as reviewed: the pristine uarch program reads main-machine memory only at shadow/PMA/TLB addresses below 0x11000, inside uarch RAM, or at guest physical addresses that passed the interpreter's PMA lookup (memory and flash/NVRAM ranges end below 2^56 per the manual; page-table walks read PTEs at PPN<<12 < 2^56 after a PMA check). TLB hits are re-verified against the PMA on every hit in the uarch bridge (do_verify_cold_tlb_slot). So no input sequence makes the pristine uarch address the last leaf; the before-state requires arbitrary uarch registers.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies (trigger is a before-state/proof in a dispute, in scope). 2 Role: machine-solidity-step = 'Referee verifier' (AUDIT.md). 3 High/Medium: Section 8 High 'A divergence between paths only at demonstrably unreachable states.' R2 lists 'Every log producer and every log verifier' and 'The on-chain verifiers' among paths that 'must agree'; R3: 'A verifier must never turn a log defect into an accepted no-op, nor a semantic no-op into a rejection' (here a semantic load becomes a rejection); R10: 'A verifier must remain memory-safe, bounded, and deterministic whatever their values' / outcome must not depend on build/implementation. Unreachable (argument above) -> High. If a reachable state could reach it, it would be Critical as an R4 completeness failure (the honest proof cannot verify on-chain).
candidates.threat_to_goal: Removes the margin that every reachable uarch transition has an on-chain-verifiable proof: if any reachable path ever made the uarch touch the top leaf, the honest operator could log the step but the referee would revert, so the honest claim would lose the uarch match by timeout (completeness failure).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R10/lastleaf.lua on the shared EVM harness (anvil 8546, StepVerifier over the regenerated step): 'ld x2,0(x1)' with x1=0xfffffffffffffff8 and x1=0xffffffffffffffe0: native log_step_uarch ok, C++ verify_step_uarch ok and equal to native root, EVM step reverted 'panic: assertion failed (0x01)'. Controls x1=0xffffffffffffffd8 and 0x00fffffffffffff8: all three accept with equal roots.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: baremetal-minimal, write 'ld x2,0(x1)' at 0x600000, uarch_pc=0x600000, uarch_x1=0xfffffffffffffff8; log = m:log_step_uarch(); assert evm_step e:step(before, log) succeeds and returns m:get_root_hash() after the step (and equals machine:verify_step_uarch). Exit 1 while the EVM reverts with Panic(0x01).

candidates.title: verify_step (main-processor step-log verifier) lets the step log select the hash function
candidates.component: C++ replay_step_state_access / machine::verify_step (cm_verify_step and its Lua/JSON-RPC bindings)
candidates.role: Support (off-chain verifier); stands in for a ZK main-step verifier, which the threat model and AUDIT.md put out of scope
candidates.location: src/replay-step-state-access.hpp:185-201 (hash_function read from the log header and used for every page/sibling hash); src/machine.cpp:2313-2329 machine::verify_step (no hash-function parameter; only root_hash_before, filename, mcycle_count)
candidates.description: The verifier takes the hash function (keccak256 or sha256) from the untrusted log header instead of from its caller. R10: 'A verifier may depend on the referee parameters, on the constants of its protocol version, and on the authenticated log data, and on nothing else'; R11: 'Each deployment fixes one hash function, which no proof can select.' The field is not authenticated by anything: the verifier only checks that the root recomputed under the log-chosen function equals root_hash_before, so a forged acceptance would need a preimage/collision across hash functions (not feasible), but the selection itself contradicts R11 and makes the outcome depend on non-referee data.
candidates.trigger: Anyone who hands a step log to a caller of verify_step: set the 8-byte hash-function field to the other function.
candidates.reachability: Any log; no machine state needed.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: likely, since 'Disputes settled by other proof forms, such as a step of the main processor verified inside a proof system, are outside its scope' and AUDIT.md excludes ZK proving; if not excluded: 2 Role: Support (off-chain verifier). 3 High/Medium: Medium only if it would be High/Critical in the role it stands in for; exploitation requires breaking the hash primitives (excluded), so no wrong acceptance -> not High. 4 n/a. 5 Low: violates R11 wording ('no proof can select') without a goal impact.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (or Out of scope as ZK)
candidates.threat_to_goal: None without a hash break; it violates R11/R10's 'nothing else' requirement and would matter if the two functions were ever used where a root under one could be confused with a root under the other.
candidates.test_idea: Produce a step log with log_step on a keccak machine, flip the hash-function field to sha256 and recompute pages/siblings under sha256 for a sha256 twin machine with the same contents; assert verify_step called for the keccak deployment refuses any log whose header names a different hash function (e.g. by an explicit hash-function parameter).

not_covered: Main-processor replay (replay_step_state_access / verify_step) under arbitrary cached TLB, PMA and shadow-register values was only read, not fuzzed; ZK path not exercised (out of scope).

No systematic differential fuzzing of the C++ uarch replay vs the Solidity step over random uarch instructions and register values (only targeted address cases); per-instruction semantic equivalence left to the replay tests and the R2 angle.
Gas boundedness of the Solidity verifiers under the real block gas limit (the EVM harness disables limits); only structural boundedness (fixed number of accesses per step) was reasoned.

Solidity compiler-setting dependence (via-IR vs legacy, optimizer) was reasoned (unchecked Buffer.peekBytes32 reads past data are neutralised by Dave's exact-consumption check) but not tested by building variants.
SendCmioResponse/UArchReset Solidity vs C++ with arbitrary iflags_Y/tohost values only reasoned (both treat any nonzero iflags_Y as yielded; isYieldedManualWith identical).

Native-side handling of arbitrary TLB/PMA values (machine::mark_write_tlb_dirty_page throwing 'TLB is corrupt', uarch bridge do_read_pma abort on corrupt PMA entries) noted but not pursued: honest-operator role, other angles.
Lua/JSON log parsers feeding the C++ verifiers were skimmed (json-util access parsing looks bounded); the Lua table->access_log conversion was not audited in detail.
Dave CartesiStateTransition/DaveConsensus input-witness logic (A3) only read as far as it concerns what the verifier reads.
